{{Use dmy dates|date=March 2024}}
The concept of '''size homotopy group''' is analogous in [[size theory]] of the classical concept of [[homotopy group]]. In order to give its definition, let us assume that a [[size pair]] <math>(M,\varphi)</math> is given, where <math>M</math> is a [[closed manifold]] of class <math>C^0\ </math> and <math>\varphi:M\to \mathbb{R}^k</math> is a [[continuous function]]. Consider the [[lexicographical order]] <math>\preceq</math> on <math>\mathbb{R}^k</math> defined by setting <math>(x_1,\ldots,x_k)\preceq(y_1,\ldots,y_k)\ </math> if and only if <math>x_1 \le y_1,\ldots, x_k \le y_k</math>. For every <math>Y\in\mathbb{R}^k</math> set <math>M_{Y}=\{Z\in\mathbb{R}^k:Z\preceq Y\}</math>.

Assume that <math>P\in M_X\ </math> and <math>X\preceq Y\ </math>. If <math>\alpha\ </math>, <math>\beta\ </math> are two paths from <math>P\ </math> to <math>P\ </math> and a [[homotopy]] from <math>\alpha\ </math> to <math>\beta\ </math>, based at <math>P\ </math>, exists in the [[topological space]] <math>M_{Y}\ </math>, then we write <math>\alpha \approx_{Y}\beta\ </math>. The '''first size homotopy group''' of the [[size pair]] <math>(M,\varphi)\ </math> computed at <math>(X,Y)\ </math> is defined to be the [[quotient set]] of the set of all [[path (topology)|path]]s from <math>P\ </math> to <math>P\ </math> in <math>M_X\ </math> with respect to the [[equivalence relation]] <math>\approx_{Y}\ </math>, endowed with the operation induced by the usual composition of based [[loop (topology)|loop]]s.<ref name="FroMu99">Patrizio Frosini, Michele Mulazzani, ''Size homotopy groups for computation of natural size distances'', Bulletin of the Belgian Mathematical Society – Simon Stevin, 6:455–464, 1999.</ref>

In other words, the '''first size homotopy group''' of the [[size pair]] <math>(M,\varphi)\ </math> computed at <math>(X,Y)\ </math> and <math>P\ </math> is the image
<math>h_{XY}(\pi_1(M_X,P))\ </math>
of the first [[homotopy group]] <math>\pi_1(M_X,P)\ </math> with base point <math>P\ </math> of the [[topological space]] <math>M_X\ </math>, when <math>h_{XY}\ </math> is the [[homomorphism]] induced by the inclusion of <math>M_X\ </math> in <math>M_Y\ </math>.

The <math>n</math>-th size homotopy group is obtained by substituting the loops based at <math>P\ </math> with the [[continuous function]]s <math>\alpha:S^n\to M\ </math> taking a fixed point of <math>S^n\ </math> to <math>P\ </math>, as happens when higher [[homotopy group]]s are defined.
